Hannah — initial triage notes:
- I pulled the traces and matched request IDs against our ingress logs. Pattern: the slow requests show elevated request queue wait times on worker nodes that handled >100 concurrent KV-cache sessions. KV cache hit rate drops to ~72% for those specific requests.
- No immediate OOMs or worker crashes in the window. No retries recorded from client side.
- Scheduler metrics show sporadic queue depth spikes on two workers (w-34, w-38) coinciding with slow traces; those workers are on the same host rack. Suspect localized queueing/backpressure when load funnels to those instances.

Short-term proposals (safe, reversible):
1) Route ClearPath’s traffic away from rack-A hosts (w-34/38) to alternate capacity for 30–60m. This is quick but requires capacity headroom. (runtime config change)
2) Enforce per-customer concurrency cap at 50 concurrent requests for ClearPath for the next 2 hours to limit queuing tail.
3) Offer a fallback routing to rwd-small-quantized (slightly lower quality) for checkout critical paths; add an opt-in header so we can track success.

I can instrument additional per-worker KV cache telemetry and surface a flamegraph within 2 hours. If we need immediate capacity, we will need an exec decision to burst more GPUs on the Dedicated pool.

-Dylan
